mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for FEDFUNDS and SPX 20d returns.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates a restrictive monetary policy phase that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate signal a monetary tightening cycle combined with labor market weakness, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS>4.5% and UNRATE>3.5%).

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates (below 3.5%) indicate a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.
